original_question: Consider a geodesic-type vector field G=g1(z)v d/dz + (nu-1)g2(z)v^2 d/dv associated to a homogeneous vector field in dimension two. Describe the local dynamics of G near an irregular singularity (zeta_0,0), i.e., where the vanishing orders satisfy mu1(zeta_0) > mu2(zeta_0)+1.
target_in_paper: Section 3.6, open problem (OP17): "Describe the local dynamics of a vector field G of the form (5) about an irregular singularity (ζ0, 0)." The surrounding paragraph defines G from a homogeneous vector field Q=(Q1,Q2) of degree ν≥2 in dimension 2 and classifies irregular singularities by the condition μ1(ζ0)>μ2(ζ0)+1. ([pagine.dm.unipi.it](https://pagine.dm.unipi.it/abate/articoli/artric/files/opendiscdynsyst.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's exact target: it uses the correct object (the vector field G of equation (5)), the correct ambient dimension (n=2), the correct singular point ((ζ0,0)), and the correct irregularity condition μ1(ζ0)>μ2(ζ0)+1. It also asks for exactly what OP17 asks for, namely a description of the local dynamics near/about that irregular singularity. ([pagine.dm.unipi.it](https://pagine.dm.unipi.it/abate/articoli/artric/files/opendiscdynsyst.pdf))
missing_details: The paper's exact term is "geodesic field," not "geodesic-type vector field." ([pagine.dm.unipi.it](https://pagine.dm.unipi.it/abate/articoli/artric/files/opendiscdynsyst.pdf))

The ambient space should be specified: G is defined on the total space of a suitable line bundle over P^1(C), written in local coordinates induced by the usual non-homogeneous coordinate centered at [1:0]∈P^1(C). ([pagine.dm.unipi.it](https://pagine.dm.unipi.it/abate/articoli/artric/files/opendiscdynsyst.pdf))

The source data should be stated explicitly: Q=(Q1,Q2) is a homogeneous vector field of degree ν≥2, with n=2. ([pagine.dm.unipi.it](https://pagine.dm.unipi.it/abate/articoli/artric/files/opendiscdynsyst.pdf))
The coefficient functions should be defined explicitly as g1(z)=Q2(1,z)-zQ1(1,z) and g2(z)=Q1(1,z). ([pagine.dm.unipi.it](https://pagine.dm.unipi.it/abate/articoli/artric/files/opendiscdynsyst.pdf))
The notation μj(ζ0) should be defined as the order of vanishing of gj at ζ0. ([pagine.dm.unipi.it](https://pagine.dm.unipi.it/abate/articoli/artric/files/opendiscdynsyst.pdf))

The geometric meaning of the point should be stated: (ζ0,0) corresponds to the direction [1:ζ0]∈P^1(C). ([pagine.dm.unipi.it](https://pagine.dm.unipi.it/abate/articoli/artric/files/opendiscdynsyst.pdf))

For full paper-faithfulness, the question should stay neutral as to whether the corresponding characteristic direction is degenerate or non-degenerate; the paper allows irregular singularities of either type. ([pagine.dm.unipi.it](https://pagine.dm.unipi.it/abate/articoli/artric/files/opendiscdynsyst.pdf))

If the question is meant to be fully stand-alone, it should say that the problem concerns local holomorphic dynamics about the singularity. ([pagine.dm.unipi.it](https://pagine.dm.unipi.it/abate/articoli/artric/files/opendiscdynsyst.pdf))
refined_question: Let Q=(Q1,Q2) be a homogeneous vector field of degree ν≥2 on C^2, and let G be the associated geodesic field on the total space of a suitable line bundle over P^1(C). In the local coordinates (z,v) induced by the usual non-homogeneous coordinate centered at [1:0]∈P^1(C), suppose G has the form G=g1(z)v∂/∂z+(ν−1)g2(z)v^2∂/∂v, where g1(z)=Q2(1,z)-zQ1(1,z) and g2(z)=Q1(1,z). For ζ0∈C, let μj(ζ0) be the order of vanishing of gj at ζ0, and assume that the point (ζ0,0), corresponding to [1:ζ0]∈P^1(C), is an irregular singularity, i.e. μ1(ζ0)>μ2(ζ0)+1. Describe the local dynamics of G about the irregular singularity (ζ0,0).
justification: The draft clearly targets Section 3.6 rather than any introductory statement: the paper first explains that, for n=2, the study of a homogeneous vector field Q can be reduced to the study of its associated geodesic field G; it then defines apparent, Fuchsian, and irregular singularities by the vanishing orders of g1 and g2; and it finally states OP17 exactly in terms of describing the local dynamics of G about an irregular singularity (ζ0,0). The immediately preceding context also explains why this is the open case: formal normal forms were obtained for all singularities, but holomorphic normal forms and detailed local dynamics were only obtained for apparent and Fuchsian singularities. The refined question therefore keeps the scope identical to OP17 and only restores the omitted setup and notation needed to make it stand-alone. ([pagine.dm.unipi.it](https://pagine.dm.unipi.it/abate/articoli/artric/files/opendiscdynsyst.pdf))
